limitations_and_boundaries: The study is limited to the Tau-P301S mouse model; generalizability to other tauopathies or human AD requires further validation.
C1q antibody rescue of synapse density was assessed only at 5 days post-injection; longer-term effects and functional outcomes (e.g., LTP, behavior) were not improved at this time point.
The proteomic analysis focused on PSD fractions from 9-month-old mice; earlier or later time points may reveal different changes.
siRNA knockdown experiments were performed in cultured hippocampal neurons, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions.
The causal link between GTPase regulatory protein loss and spine loss is inferred from knockdown and pharmacological rescue; direct genetic rescue in Tau-P301S mice was not performed.
Microglial engulfment was assessed by confocal imaging of fixed tissue; dynamic live imaging was not performed.
The study does not address whether C1q tagging is specific to Tau pathology or also occurs in other neurodegenerative conditions.
